persona.name: Walter Greene
persona.description: Walter Greene is a 72-year-old retired African-American janitor living alone with a history of heart failure and multiple related hospitalizations, making him a frequent flier in the outpatient clinic. He is grumpy and blunt but has a dry sense of humor, and he openly dislikes students and trainees. He is noncompliant with his cardiac diet but warms up considerably when conversation turns to his work history or when he feels respected by clinical staff. He presents a significant counseling challenge for dietetics students, requiring strong rapport-building skills, motivational interviewing, and practical sodium- and fluid-restricted dietary guidance tailored to an older adult living alone on a fixed income.
persona.cultural_context: Southern-influenced food traditions; comfort foods such as cured meats, canned goods, and seasoned dishes are culturally significant. Fixed income limits food choices. Strong sense of independence and self-reliance; may resist being told what to do by younger or unfamiliar clinicians.
persona.personality: Grumpy, blunt, and initially dismissive, especially toward students and trainees. Has a dry, self-deprecating sense of humor that emerges once he feels comfortable. Proud of his work history and life experience. Values respect and directness over pleasantries.
persona.communication_style: Terse and guarded at first; uses humor and sarcasm to deflect. Opens up significantly when asked about his past work or life experiences. Responds poorly to being lectured or talked down to. Engages more when the student listens more than they talk.
persona.support_system: Limited formal support; occasional visits from an adult child who lives out of town. Friendly with a few neighbors. Strong relationship with clinic nursing staff and physical therapist.
persona.readiness_to_change: Pre-contemplative to contemplative; resistant to dietary changes but acknowledges hospitalizations are disruptive. May shift toward action if approached with respect and practical, low-burden strategies.

settings.encounter_goal: Nutrition assessment and counseling (Nutrition Care Process)

faculty_brief.notes: Noncompliant with diet but loves "talking shop" with PT and nurses.

objectives.objective: Establish rapport with a resistant older adult patient using respectful, patient-centered communication.

expected_discoveries.text: Patient is initially dismissive of students and requires a non-defensive, respectful approach
Asking about his work history and life experience helps him open up
Avoiding a lecturing tone is essential to keeping him engaged
Humor and directness, when used appropriately, build trust with this patient

possible_patient_reactions: May open with a sarcastic comment about being seen by a student again
Will test the student with blunt remarks to see how they respond under pressure
Warms noticeably if the student asks a genuine question about his life or work
May disengage or shut down if he feels he is being talked down to

objectives.objective: Conduct a thorough dietary recall and identify key sources of excess sodium and fluid in the patient's diet.

expected_discoveries.text: Canned soups, deli meats, and seasoned convenience foods are primary sodium sources
Sweet tea consumed throughout the day contributes significantly to fluid intake
Patient does not track fluid intake and is unaware of how much he consumes
Skipping meals leads to larger, saltier meals later in the day
Ibuprofen use is an additional concern for fluid retention and kidney function

possible_patient_reactions: May minimize or underreport food intake initially
Will become more forthcoming about diet details once he feels the student is not judging him
May express frustration that everything he enjoys is on the restricted list

objectives.objective: Develop a practical, individualized medical nutrition therapy plan for heart failure in an older adult living alone on a fixed income.

expected_discoveries.text: Standard 2g sodium and 1.5L fluid restriction recommendations need to be translated into concrete, affordable food swaps
Patient needs low-burden strategies that do not require extensive cooking for one person
Low-sodium canned goods and seasoning alternatives can address both cost and taste concerns
Fluid restriction counseling must address sweet tea specifically as a culturally preferred beverage

possible_patient_reactions: Will resist any plan that feels like total deprivation of preferred foods
More receptive to small, specific changes than an overhaul of his entire diet
May ask pointed questions about cost and practicality that the student must be prepared to answer

objectives.objective: Apply motivational interviewing techniques to explore ambivalence and identify the patient's own reasons for change.

expected_discoveries.text: Fear of rehospitalization and loss of independence are the patient's strongest motivators
Patient has demonstrated capacity for behavior change by quitting smoking
Ambivalence is present: he dislikes hospitalizations but also dislikes dietary restrictions
Eliciting his own words about what he wants to avoid is more effective than providing external reasons

possible_patient_reactions: May initially respond to open-ended questions with short, dismissive answers
Will engage more deeply if the student reflects his stated values back to him
May surprise the student with candid self-awareness once trust is established

objectives.objective: Recognize the intersection of medication adherence and dietary behavior in heart failure management and communicate concerns appropriately.

expected_discoveries.text: Patient skips furosemide to avoid urinary urgency, directly contributing to fluid retention and edema
Ibuprofen use is contraindicated given CKD and heart failure and should be flagged for the supervising clinician
Inconsistent metformin use is tied to irregular meal patterns
Student should understand the dietitian's role in flagging medication-nutrition interactions and coordinating with the care team

possible_patient_reactions: May be defensive when diuretic skipping is raised
Will likely not volunteer ibuprofen use unless specifically asked about over-the-counter medications
May be receptive to a practical suggestion about timing the diuretic to fit his schedule

objectives.objective: Address social determinants of health and identify community or interprofessional resources to support dietary adherence in an isolated older adult.

expected_discoveries.text: Patient lives alone with limited social support, which affects meal preparation and motivation
Loneliness contributes to eating out at fast food restaurants as a form of social engagement
Community resources such as Meals on Wheels, senior center meal programs, or food pantries with low-sodium options may be appropriate
Coordination with the clinic social worker and the patient's existing rapport with nursing and PT staff can support a team-based approach

possible_patient_reactions: May initially reject the idea of meal delivery programs as charity or a sign of dependence
Could be open to senior center programs if framed around social connection rather than need
May respond well if the student acknowledges his independence while presenting options as tools, not crutches

Anthropometrics, vital signs, and laboratory values are plausible estimates consistent with a decompensated heart failure patient with CKD and diabetes; none were provided by faculty.

Ibuprofen OTC use was added as a realistic and clinically significant finding for an older adult with joint pain, CKD, and heart failure; it was not specified by faculty.
Southern-influenced dietary pattern assumed based on African-American cultural background and age cohort; this is a plausible assumption and not a stereotype, but should be confirmed in simulation.
